Zero to four weeks: No trouble at all. You're probably only in tourist traps and you will end up paying more than the locals sometimes but you'll have a great time. It's a friendly country with a shitload of activities and history. Everyone is kind and helpful and understanding.

One to five months: You're there for a long time. You may learn that a lot of apartment agencies and some other services reuse service to a foreigner, especially one who doesn't' speak Japanese. Disillusionment, but it's still a great place. Everyone is so polite! You've started to learn that some people idolize foreigners, some hate them, and most are somewhere in between. You now shop at some of the same places locals shop, and you're learning which places cost more.

Five months to a year: You're in for the long haul, and if you're not studying Japanese fuck you. You learn the sarcasm behind some of the politeness. Culture clashes. Severe culture shock hits you at eight months. WTF Japan? There are too many concrete buildings, not enough maps, the few street signs are all in kanji you can't read, and everything is too small, too gray, and too close. Money is important and you've had to get a Japanese bank account. Transferring money is expensive unless you have a lot of it or you've been doing business in Japan for years.

One to three years: You have definitely been refused service by multiple apartment agencies. You cannot find work except as an English monkey. (because you haven't learned Japanese) You're learning where and how to get money to and from overseas without paying an arm and a leg. You probably have one or two Japanese friends. You understand a lot more about Japanese culture and you fucking hate it. Two faced sarcastic assholes.

Three to ten years: You've picked up some Japanese despite yourself and you are familiar with your area and your local City Hall. You know how local, prefecture, and federal taxes are paid. You understand how work visas work. You're becoming familiar with the job market for foreigners and how it's different. Either you stay in friendly places all the time (in which your opinions haven't changed) or you've pushed out of your comfort zone many, many times. (Japanese people aren't assholes, I was an asshole. I wanted them to conform to my culture and that just didn't make sense. There's an ebb and a flow: a give and take.)

Ten tears and on: You speak fluent Japanese and have job prospects beyond being an English monkey. You're working on immigrating. Japan has a deep, rich culture but you miss home. You get by with making or ordering foods you can't normally get. Inside your head you mock new foreigners but you have come to learn no matter how Japanese you become you'll never truly be accepted.
